Hi Sofia / John —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: 

Summary from today's call:
- Objective: Evaluate Redwood Private for hosting inference in AcmeHealth VPC / potential air-gapped deployment.
- Key concerns: control-plane reachability, customer-managed KMS, network egress constraints, audit logs/SOC2 evidence, and throughput/latency vs Bedrock/Vertex.
- Decision makers: John (CTO), Sofia (Prod Ops), Infra Eng team (technical validation).

Proposed next steps (we suggest the following test matrix):
1) Networking connectivity check (can Redwood control plane be reached from your environment) — quick TCP/https handshake test.
2) Air-gap feasibility: describe minimal inbound/outbound requirements; validate whether our private control plane can be replaced with fully customer-hosted control plane option for an air-gapped PoC.
3) KMS/integration test: verify HSM/KMS scenarios and key management restrictions.
4) Performance baseline: small inference benchmark (text-generation QPS and p99 latency) comparing Redwood Private vs your existing hyperscaler endpoints.

Who we'll involve: Marissa (Solutions Eng) will lead the private deployment checklist and coordinate with your infra team. I've attached a short brief comparing Redwood vs common hyperscalers and a networking checklist to speed the validation.

Proposed schedule:
- Network checklist and access info from Acme by EOD Monday 2026-09-13
- PoC kickoff (workshop + SRE pairing) week of 2026-09-20

Questions for you now:
- Can your infra team share a point-of-contact and available windows for the network handshake?
- Any regulatory blockers we should be aware of for an air-gapped PoC?

Thanks — I'll follow up internally to loop in SRE and get the PoC plan ready.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC/air-gap) — answers + proposed test matrix

Hi Sofia — thanks, and great availability for the network window. Answers inline below and next steps.

1) Control plane / air-gap: We support multiple private deployment modes. For most customers we run a Redwood-managed control plane that communicates with your deployed inference nodes over TLS. For air-gapped requirements, we offer a fully customer-hosted control plane option (on-prem or in your VPC) in our Private product — in that mode there are zero outbound connections to Redwood-managed endpoints. We'll need to validate operability of features you want (metrics, rollouts) when the control plane is customer-hosted; Marissa will map those feature gaps.

2) KMS / HSM: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. Keys can be stored and used within your HSM/KMS (we support KMIP and common cloud KMS APIs). We can ensure the platform never exports plaintext keys. We'll document the KMS flow for your security team.

3) Perf benchmarks: Good call on being explicit. For the comparison brief I attached: we used the following reference points — Bedrock: c6g.8xlarge + model X-1.3B; Vertex: A2-highgpu-1g + model Y-1.5B; Redwood Private: r-infer.rtxA6000 (3rd-party tuned) + Redwood-optimized quantized variants. We'll run your 1k-token workload for p95/p99 and raw tokens-per-second under identical batch sizes. Marissa, will you own the perf script and provide the specific command line and model weights?

Proposed test matrix we will run during the workshop:
- Network: TCP/HTTPS handshake, port reachability, and a quick TLS cert validation (15–30 min).
- Control plane: deploy a customer-hosted control plane in a test subnet and validate registration of a single inference node.
- KMS: demo encrypt/decrypt flow with a customer-managed key.
- Perf: run 3x passes of the 1k-token workload, record p50/p95/p99 and throughput.

I've attached a networking checklist to the shared Drive and will upload the perf script beforehand.

Marissa / Aditya — please confirm you'll join the Tue 09/14 network window and prepare the perf script + instructions.

Thanks,
Vanessa
